target_customer: Healthcare providers and provider groups (specialty practices, infusion, DME, hospitals) that receive patient referrals by fax and PDF
problem: Referrals between providers arrive as faxes and multi-page PDFs in thousands of formats and a person must read and key them in, so patients fall into a black hole before scheduling.
business_model: B2B SaaS for healthcare administrative teams, configured per provider
product_category: Healthcare AI referral intake and patient flow automation

founders.name: Trey Holterman
education: Computer science major, school not named on YC page
founders.background_notes: Former All-American rower per YC page; former teaching assistant.

founders.name: Diego Baugh
founders.background_notes: Stanford rowing team per YC page.

founders.name: Tyler Johnson
prior_employers: Technical consulting (one year, employer not named)
founders.background_notes: YC page says the founders met at Stanford.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading handwritten, multi-page faxes in thousands of layouts needed a purpose-trained model; the founders built RaeLM (7B, trained on 3M+ documents per the YC page) before the 2023 LLM wave.

defensibility.rationale: Document corpus and per-provider workflow configuration add lock-in, but the underlying approach could be copied by EHR vendors or other AI intake startups.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition found as of the sources checked; Tennr raised a Series C in June 2025 and kept growing.

market_need_then: YC page states about 90 percent of provider to provider communication still ran over fax, and staff retyped referrals manually, a large labor cost and patient leakage problem.

branding.domain_note: Uses tennr.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, outcome-focused healthcare ops language such as frictionless patient flow on the homepage.

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of meme or merch culture found; coverage is trade and business press.

brand_strength.rationale: No source shows brand-led growth; coverage focuses on funding and product, and the name origin is not public.

outcome_analysis: Tennr targeted a concrete, ugly workflow, fax referral intake, with a purpose-trained model and sold it to providers who measure lost patients. It raised an $18M Series A in March 2024, a $37M Series B in October 2024 and a $101M Series C at a reported $605M valuation in June 2025, with the company saying revenue more than tripled after the Series B. The homepage now claims 200+ provider customers. No acquisition or distress was found.
notes: Series C figures confirmed by several outlets (Fortune, Fierce, MobiHealthNews, SiliconANGLE). Series A and B were seen in search result snippets from trade outlets; the Series B lead is from one result. A $500K pre-seed in April 2023 appears only in one aggregator and is unverified. Competitor searches returned only 2025 to 2026 aggregator lists, so no dated competitors near the batch are recorded. Founding year conflicts across sources (2021 YC and CB Insights, 2019 per one VC page). Fierce article returned HTTP 403 and was not read.
